Re-audited 2026-08-23 (deep wreck research): the prior note's claim that 'myscubadivinggearguide.com does reference a Blue Diamond wreck in the Providencia context' was checked against the CURRENT live page and is FALSE - that page's only wreck is called 'Planchon', with no mention of 'Blue Diamond'. PADI confirms 'Blue Diamond'/Barco Hundido is a specific, well-documented wreck located at San Andres island, coordinates 12.53547,-81.73594 (roughly 50km from Providencia) - not this destination. Cross-checked against FIVE independent sources for the Providencia-area wreck, all of which name it 'El Planchon'/'Planchon' (never 'Blue Diamond'): myscubadivinggearguide.com (WWII submarine supply ship, 15m, hull side up), PADI Spanish site page for 'el-planchon-2' (coords 13.37167,-81.41796, WWII-era cargo tanker, upside down), travelandiving.com ('Planchon de Providencia', sharks/morays/barracuda regulars), The Dive Shop Old Providence (18-24m, WWII cargo oil tanker), and Felipe Diving Center (50ft/15m, 'German WWII oil tanker wreck'). No source anywhere names a Providencia wreck 'Blue Diamond'. Conclusion: this entry's name is very likely a mislabeling - either confused with the San Andres 'Blue Diamond', or a locally-used alias not attested in any source checked. Left unvalidated; vessel name is NOT confirmed, so build date/length/tonnage/sinking cause cannot be cross-checked for THIS name and are not stated. Coordinates/depth are plausibly consistent with the same wreck multiple sources call El Planchon, but that identity is not confirmed either - not renamed without a source that explicitly links these coordinates to that name.
